You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
Which type of good does not consume scarce resources?

options.B: free good
options.C: merit good
options.D: public good

questions.questionText: The factors of production earn different rewards. What identifies the correct economic term for these rewards?

options.B: enterprise – dividends
options.C: labour – interest
options.D: land – rents

questions.questionText: What is most likely to be an advantage of the division of labour?

options.A: an increase in labour force creativity
options.B: an increase in labour productivity
options.C: an increase in workforce flexibility
options.D: an increase in worker satisfaction

questions.questionText: A government wishes to encourage the consumption of a merit good and reduce the consumption of a demerit good. Which policy should it adopt towards each good? merit good demerit good

options.A: impose a minimum price produce only in the public sector
options.B: increase advertising on the benefits put legal controls on output of the good
options.C: confine access to certain age groups tax output
options.D: subsidise the good set a minimum level of output

questions.questionText: Shoe manufacturers often use leather to make their most expensive shoes. Due to a world shortage of leather, the price of leather has risen. What will be the effect of this price change?

options.A: The demand curve for leather shoes will shift to the left.
options.B: The demand curve for a substitute for leather shoes will shift to the right.
options.C: The supply curve for leather shoes will shift to the right.
options.D: The supply curve for a substitute for leather to make expensive shoes will shift to the right.

questions.questionText: The Chinese government relaxed controls on private house ownership. Private house ownership rose sharply, replacing demand for apartments rented from the state. What would have been most likely to happen to private house prices and the rents of apartments? private house apartment prices rents

options.B: decrease increase
options.C: increase decrease
options.D: increase increase

questions.questionText: The supply, S, of a product is determined by the equation S = 10 + 10P, when P is the price of the product. What is the price elasticity of supply when the price changes from $1 to $2?
A good has the following elasticity values. cross elasticity of demand +1.4 income elasticity of demand –0.8 Which statement is correct?

options.A: The good is a complement and inferior.
options.B: The good is a complement and normal.
options.C: The good is a substitute and inferior.
options.D: The good is a substitute and normal.

questions.questionText: Different areas on the diagram represent different aspects of a market. S price R T S U E F D O G H I quantity Which row correctly identifies the three variables shown? consumer producer total consumer surplus surplus expenditure

options.B: RST UST STGO
options.C: RTU UTE STGO
options.D: RTEU TEF RFU

questions.questionText: Which combination of the classification of a good and market change will cause the demand curve for the good to shift to the right? classification of good market change

options.B: inferior good price decrease
options.C: normal good income decrease
options.D: normal good price decrease

questions.questionText: Which policy is most likely to solve the free rider problem caused by public goods?

options.B: a direct provision by the government
options.C: a minimum price
options.D: a tax on a substitute good

questions.questionText: Very low interest rates in an economy encourage economic growth and cause a large increase in house prices. Which group of people is most likely to experience a fall in income and an increase in wealth as a result of these changes?

options.A: retired people living in rented houses
options.B: retired people who own their houses
options.C: young people buying their own houses
options.D: young people living with their parents

questions.questionText: A large-scale farming enterprise uses inputs of labour and capital equipment that are substitutes. If the government introduces a policy to subsidise capital equipment, how would this affect the factor inputs? quantity of quantity of capital labour equipment

options.B: decreases decreases
options.C: increases decreases
options.D: increases increases

questions.questionText: A country experienced an annual deflation rate of 2% for four successive years. Which statement is correct for the four-year period?

options.B: The price level fell by less than 8%.
options.C: The real value of money fell by 8%.
options.D: The real value of money fell by less than 8%.

questions.questionText: In the circular flow of income model of an economy, Y, C, I, G, X, S, T and M represent total income, consumption, investment, government expenditure, exports, saving, taxation and imports respectively. Which statement is correct?

options.A: At equilibrium, the levels of Y and C are always the same.
options.B: Governments always adjust G so that the economy is in equilibrium.
options.C: If I is not equal to S, it is still possible for the national income to be in equilibrium.
options.D: If the national income is in equilibrium, X must be equal to M.

questions.questionText: What leads to a rise in frictional unemployment?

options.A: an economy moving into a period of recession
options.B: replacement of workers with computers in the service sector
options.C: a change from an agriculturally based economy to an industrial economy
options.D: a rise in the number of workers leaving one job to look for another job

questions.questionText: The information shows data from a country’s national income accounts. $ million gross domestic product at market prices 200000 gross value added at basic prices 180000 subsidies 5000 capital consumption 30000 What can be concluded from the income accounts? net domestic product indirect tax revenue at market prices $ million $ million

A government is considering building a large hospital. The impact on the country’s price level will depend partly on the amount of expensive raw materials the country imports for the hospital and the level of unemployment in the country. Which combination of imports of materials for the hospital and the level of unemployment is most likely to lead to the largest rise in the price level? imports of unemployment materials

options.B: high low
options.C: low high
options.D: low low

questions.questionText: If interest rates are reduced, what is most likely to decrease?

options.B: consumer spending
options.C: import prices
options.D: export prices

questions.questionText: Supply-side policy often has fiscal consequences. Which statement is not correct?

options.A: Increased government spending supporting technical progress has beneficial long-term supply-side effects but may have short-term inflationary consequences.
options.B: Increased government expenditure on training increases a country’s long-run aggregate supply (LRAS) and also has an expansionary effect on aggregate demand (AD).
options.C: Reduced government infrastructure spending reduces an economy’s LRAS and has a short-term expansionary effect on AD.
options.D: Reduced rates of tax on higher incomes increases an economy’s LRAS and has an expansionary effect on AD.

questions.questionText: Changes in fiscal policy can affect the distribution of income and wealth. Which combination of fiscal policy would most likely be regressive?

options.A: a fall in the lowest level of income when income tax has to be paid and a fall in the rate of inheritance tax
options.B: a fall in the charge made for visits to a doctor and a rise in the level of unemployment benefit
options.C: a rise in the rate of income tax charged at higher levels of income and a rise in the standard rate of corporation tax
options.D: a rise in the standard rate of income tax and a fall in the standard rate of goods and services tax

questions.questionText: What does it mean when a government has a budget surplus?

options.B: Imports exceed exports.
options.C: The government has an expansionary fiscal policy.
options.D: The national debt is increasing.

questions.questionText: A country subsidises domestic production of manufactured goods. What is the most likely outcome?

options.B: a rise in imports of manufactured goods
options.C: a rise in the rate of inflation
options.D: a rise in unemployment

questions.questionText: What is not a valid explanation of why a government might allow a deficit on the balance of payments current account to continue?

options.A: The balance of payments account must always balance.
options.B: Foreign direct investment might help to finance the deficit.
options.C: The country may have a larger surplus on the other parts of its balance of payments account.
options.D: The standard of living is increased if the level of cheap food imports is significant.

questions.questionText: A country currently producing at point X on its production possibility curve decides to specialise in the manufacture of cars and import trucks. It finds it can import one truck in exchange for four cars. trucks X 0 5000 10 000 cars What is the result in the domestic market if it exports all the extra cars?

options.B: 1000 extra trucks
options.C: 1250 extra trucks
options.D: 2000 extra trucks

questions.questionText: What is most likely to cause a current account deficit?

options.A: a recession in the domestic economy
options.B: a relatively high rate of inflation
options.C: an undervalued exchange rate
options.D: high labour productivity

questions.questionText: Two statements describing forms of protectionism a government can use are listed.
When is there an improvement in a country’s terms of trade?

options.A: when the price of exports falls more than the price of imports
options.B: when there is no change in the price of exports but a fall in the price of imports
options.C: when the value of exports increases relative to the total value of imports
options.D: when the volume of exports increases relative to the total volume of imports

questions.questionText: What is likely to happen if there is a rise in the international value of a country’s currency?

options.A: a fall in the foreign currency price of its exports
options.B: a fall in the volume of its exports
options.C: a rise in the domestic currency price of its imports
options.D: a rise in the domestic price level reasonable effort has been made by the publisher (UCLES) to trace copyright holders, but if any items requiring clearance have unwittingly been included, the publisher will be pleased to make amends at the earliest possible opportunity.
